1.name: Simple Assignment
1.description: Basic assignment operation without loops. This type of algorithm is classified as 'unknown' since it has no complex control structures.
1.note: Will be classified as 'unknown' in the analysis (no complex loops)

2.name: Simple Array Access
2.description: Direct access to an array element. Constant-time operation without loops.
2.note: Will be classified as 'unknown' in the analysis

3.name: Linear Search
3.description: Traverses an array sequentially looking for a specific element. The simplest search algorithm, ideal for small or unsorted arrays.
3.complexity: Best: O(1), Worst: O(n), Avg: O(n/2)

4.name: Iterative Binary Search
4.description: Searches for an element in a sorted array by halving the search space at each iteration. Iterative version of binary search.
4.complexity: Best: O(1), Worst: O(log n), Avg: O(log n)

5.name: Iterative Factorial
5.description: Computes the factorial of a number iteratively. More efficient than the recursive version and has no stack overflow risk for large numbers.

6.name: Array Sum
6.description: Computes the sum of all elements in an array. Simple linear algorithm that traverses the array once.

7.name: Array Maximum
7.description: Finds the maximum element in an array. Traverses the array comparing each element with the current maximum.
7.complexity: Best: O(n), Worst: O(n), Avg: O(n)

8.name: Greatest Common Divisor - Euclid's Algorithm
8.description: Computes the greatest common divisor of two numbers using Euclid's algorithm. One of the oldest and most efficient algorithms, with logarithmic complexity.

9.name: Bubble Sort
9.description: Sorts an array by comparing adjacent elements and swapping them if they are in the wrong order. One of the simplest sorting algorithms, but also one of the least efficient.
9.complexity: Best: O(n), Worst: O(n²), Avg: O(n²)

10.name: Insertion Sort
10.description: Builds the sorted array by inserting each element in its correct position. Efficient for small or nearly sorted arrays, with better performance than Bubble Sort in practice.
10.complexity: Best: O(n), Worst: O(n²), Avg: O(n²)

11.name: Selection Sort
11.description: Finds the minimum element and places it in its final position in each iteration. Performs fewer swaps than Bubble Sort, but has the same time complexity.

12.name: Recursive Fibonacci
12.description: Computes the nth Fibonacci number using direct recursion. Now analyzed with the Characteristic Equation method because T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) is a linear recurrence with constant shifts. Automatically detects that it is a linear Dynamic Programming case.
12.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

13.name: Tower of Hanoi
13.description: Solves the classic Tower of Hanoi problem using recursion. Analyzed with the Characteristic Equation method because T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1 is a linear recurrence. Automatically detects that it is a linear Dynamic Programming case.
13.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

14.name: Recursive Factorial
14.description: Computes the factorial of a number using recursion. Analyzed with the iteration method because the recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1) does not divide uniformly.

15.name: Recursive Binary Search
15.description: Searches for an element in a sorted array using recursion. Analyzed with the Master Theorem because T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1) with a=1, b=2.
15.complexity: Best: O(1), Worst: O(log n), Avg: O(log n)

16.name: MergeSort
16.description: Divide and conquer sorting algorithm that divides the array into two halves, sorts each half recursively and merges them. Analyzed with the Recursion Tree method because T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n with a=2, b=2.
16.note: Analyzed with Recursion Tree method (a=2, b=2)

17.name: Unequal Divide Algorithm
17.description: Divides a problem into 3 equal subproblems. Analyzed with the Recursion Tree method because T(n) = 3T(n/3) + 1 with a=3, b=3.
17.note: Analyzed with Recursion Tree method (a=3, b=3)

18.name: Quaternary Algorithm
18.description: Divides a problem into 4 equal subproblems. Analyzed with the Recursion Tree method because T(n) = 4T(n/4) + 1 with a=4, b=4.
18.note: Analyzed with Recursion Tree method (a=4, b=4)

19.name: QuickSort
19.description: Divide and conquer sorting algorithm using partitioning. In the best case, analyzed with the Recursion Tree method because T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n with a=2, b=2.
19.complexity: Best: O(n log n), Worst: O(n²), Avg: O(n log n)
19.note: In best case analyzed with Recursion Tree method (a=2, b=2)

20.name: N-Step Stairs (Climbing Stairs)
20.description: Counts the number of ways to climb n steps, being able to take steps of 1 or 2 at a time. Linear recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2). Analyzed with Characteristic Equation and automatically detects linear DP.
20.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

21.name: Decode Ways
21.description: Counts the number of ways to decode a numeric message where each digit or pair of digits can represent a letter. Linear recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) with conditions. Analyzed with Characteristic Equation.
21.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

22.name: Tiling 2xN (Dominoes)
22.description: Counts the number of ways to fill a 2xN board with domino tiles (2x1). Linear recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2). Analyzed with Characteristic Equation and detects linear DP.
22.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

23.name: Tribonacci
23.description: Computes the nth Tribonacci number (similar to Fibonacci but sums the last 3 terms). Linear recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3). Analyzed with Characteristic Equation.
23.complexity: O(rⁿ) where r is the largest real root of the characteristic equation
23.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

24.name: Pell Numbers
24.description: Computes the nth Pell number using the recurrence P(n) = 2P(n-1) + P(n-2). Homogeneous linear recurrence. Analyzed with Characteristic Equation.
24.note: Analyzed with Characteristic Equation (linear DP detected)

25.name: QuickSort (Average Case)
25.description: Divide and conquer sorting algorithm that works by choosing a pivot and dividing the array into two parts. In the average case, T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) but the pivot does not divide exactly in half. Analyzed only with Master Theorem because a=1 does not meet the Recursion Tree conditions.
25.complexity: Best: O(n log n), Worst: O(n²), Avg: O(n log n)
25.note: Analyzed only with Master Theorem (a=1, non-uniform divide)

26.name: Binary Search Tree Search
26.description: Searches for an element in a BST. The recurrence T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1) depends on the tree height. Analyzed only with Master Theorem because a=1, b=2 does not meet the Recursion Tree conditions.
26.complexity: Best: O(log n), Worst: O(n), Avg: O(log n)
26.note: Analyzed only with Master Theorem (a=1, b=2, average case)

27.name: Recursive Fast Exponentiation
27.description: Computes x^n efficiently using divide and conquer. T(n) = T(n/2) + O(1). Analyzed only with Master Theorem because a=1, b=2.
27.note: Analyzed only with Master Theorem (a=1, b=2)

28.name: Recursive Array Sum
28.description: Sums array elements recursively processing one element at a time. Recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1). Analyzed only with iterative method because it is not linear with multiple constant shifts.
28.note: Analyzed only with iterative method (T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1))

29.name: Linked List Search
29.description: Searches for an element in a linked list recursively. Recurrence T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1). Analyzed only with iterative method.
29.note: Analyzed only with iterative method (T(n) = T(n-1) + O(1))

30.name: Recursive Array Reverse
30.description: Reverses an array recursively by swapping elements from the ends. Recurrence T(n) = T(n-2) + O(1). Analyzed only with iterative method because it does not meet the characteristic equation conditions.
30.note: Analyzed only with iterative method (T(n) = T(n-2) + O(1))
